# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 10 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 10
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Since Moses said: "You shall not eat swine, nor eagle, nor hawk, nor raven, nor any fish that does not have scales" — he received three doctrines in his understanding.
2. Moreover he says to them in Deuteronomy: "And I will make my statutes a covenant with this people." The commandment of God is therefore not regarding the abstaining from food; but Moses spoke in the Spirit.
3. He mentioned the swine for this reason: do not associate with people who are like pigs — who, when they are in want, forget the Lord, but when they are satisfied, they remember the Lord; just as the pig, when eating, does not know its master, but when it is hungry it cries out, and when it receives food it is silent again.
4. "Neither shalt thou eat the eagle, nor the hawk, nor the kite, nor the raven." You shall not, he says, associate with or imitate such men who do not know how to gain their food by labor and sweat, but who violently seize other men's possessions, while they are careful to appear to be walking in innocence, and watch around them for those whom they may rob in their greed — just as these birds do not procure food for themselves by labor, but sit idle and seek to eat the meat of others, being destructive in their wickedness.
5. "And you shall not eat," he says, "the lamprey, nor the polypus, nor the cuttlefish." You shall not, he says, become like such men — who are utterly ungodly and condemned already, and who cling to the world as though it were something desirable; just as these fish alone are accursed and lurk in the deep, not swimming as the others do but dwelling in the mud beneath the deep water.
6. Furthermore, "You shall not eat the hare." Why? Do not become a corrupter of children, nor like such people; because the hare adds an additional opening each year, and so has as many holes as it is years old.
7. "Neither shalt thou eat the hyena." Do not become, he says, an adulterer or a corruptor, or become like such persons. Why? Because this animal changes its nature year by year, and becomes at one time male and at another female.
8. And he hated the weasel also and with good reason. Do not become like those who we hear commit lawlessness with the mouth, and do not associate with unclean women who work iniquity with the mouth; for this animal conceives through the mouth.
9. These things Moses received as spiritual commandments. But they, because of the lust of the flesh, took them as referring to food.
10. But David also received the knowledge of the three doctrines, and says in like manner: "Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly and did not take his stand in the way of sinners" — just as the fish who go into the deep in darkness — "and did not sit in the seat of the scornful" — just as those birds which sit and wait for prey.
11. You now have the teaching concerning food in its fullness.
